2_Introduction: The device showed the highest certified PCE of 19.4054%, with VOC of 1.0765 V, JSC of 23.681 mA/cm², and FF of 76.1217%.The device shows a maximum PCE of 19.4054%, with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.0765 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 23.681 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 76.1217%. For the perovskite composition Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2, 1.5 mol/L perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1200 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. The crystallization process was refined by injecting 200 µL of antisolvent at last 8 s during spin-coating. The film was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation (Cs⁺ enhancing phase stability and suppressing halide segregation, FA⁺ enabling optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor ~0.91 and narrow bandgap ~1.53 eV), Pb²⁺ at the B-site ensuring strong orbital overlap for high carrier mobility, and I⁻/Br⁻ anion mixing tuning lattice strain and defect energetics—undergoes highly controlled crystallization governed by the precise interplay of precursor concentration (1.5 mol/L, balancing nucleation density and solute availability), dual-speed spin-coating (1200 rpm for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm for rapid solvent expulsion), antisolvent quenching (200 µL injected at the critical 8 s mark to induce instantaneous supersaturation and homogeneous nucleation while suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening), and thermal annealing (110 °C for 30 min, sufficient to drive off residual DMSO/DMF without decomposing FA⁺ or volatilizing Br⁻, thereby consolidating grain boundaries and healing point defects such as undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies). Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the Cs/FA mixed-cation system synergizes with the kinetic control of crystallization to minimize deep-level trap states: the optimized antisolvent timing suppresses PbI₂-rich amorphous intermediates and residual δ-phase impurities, while the moderate annealing temperature avoids excessive halide loss that would otherwise generate iodine interstitials or lead-halide antisites. This is corroborated structurally by XRD evidence—absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and sharp, symmetric (110) and (220) reflections with narrow FWHM—indicating high phase purity, minimal microstrain, and large, well-oriented crystallites; optically, the high PL intensity and long carrier lifetime (implied by the elevated VOC and FF) reflect suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways arising from reduced trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination at grain boundaries and surfaces; morphologically, uniform film coverage and high grayscale homogeneity in optical/PL mapping confirm continuous, pinhole-free morphology essential for lateral charge transport and interfacial contact integrity. Collectively, these crystallization- and composition-engineered structural, optical, and morphological advantages yield VOC of 1.0765 V, JSC of 23.681 mA/cm², FF of 76.1217%, and PCE of 19.4054%.
